finding.claim: GET /rss fetches an attacker-supplied URL with no scheme or host validation and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the requester (non-blind SSRF, unauthenticated).
finding.source: Query parameter u on GET /rss (app.rb:8, params[:u])

trace.note: get "/rss" route; no auth or before-filter
URI.open(params[:u]).read performs the HTTP(S) request to the attacker-chosen URL
data[0, 400] returned in the HTTP response body

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local address rejection. open-uri follows redirects by default, so any check on the initial URL alone would be bypassed by a 30x to an internal target. Response body is returned, so the attacker gets read access, not just a blind request.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check is the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:13-14, but it is in the /trusted route, not /rss. The /rss handler (app.rb:7-9) has no auth, scheme, host, or private-address check before URI.open at app.rb:8.
verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query parameter params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns data[0, 400] to the caller, so the claim holds as a non-blind SSRF; the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 and app.rb:14 guards only the separate /trusted route. The candidate's trace is accurate (lines 7, 8, 9). A side note that strengthens the finding: URI.open also falls back to local file opening for non-URI strings, so a plain path such as /etc/passwd may be readable too.
